summary:
SPHEREx SkyTime is a web-based astronomical data exploration platform designed to make NASA's SPHEREx observations easier to access, visualize, and understand.

The platform connects to the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) to retrieve real SPHEREx Data Release 1 (DR1) observation metadata and astronomical image files. It processes FITS-format scientific data into browser-viewable images and provides an interactive interface for exploring observations using sky coordinates and spectral information.

The project aims to simplify access to infrared astronomical observations, support comparative exploration of the universe, and make scientific space data more accessible to students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts.
details:
SPHEREx SkyTime – Exploring a Changing Universe

SPHEREx SkyTime is a web-based astronomy exploration platform designed to help users explore infrared observations collected by NASA's SPHEREx mission. It retrieves astronomical observation records from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive using user-entered sky coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination). The platform displays real SPHEREx image data and allows users to view and compare different image products from the same observed region.

The project aims to make astronomical data easier to access and understand. Instead of requiring users to manually search through complex scientific archives and FITS files, SPHEREx SkyTime provides a simple interface where users can enter sky coordinates, retrieve available observations, and view processed astronomical images. This can support students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers in exploring infrared sky data.

The intended impact is to improve public access to space-science data, encourage interest in astronomy, and provide a foundation for studying how astronomical objects and regions change over time. In future development, the platform aims to support observations from different dates, image blinking, image-difference analysis, and the identification of possible moving-object candidates. These advanced analysis features are planned and are not yet fully implemented.

The project was developed using React.js and JavaScript for the frontend, HTML and CSS for the user interface, and Python with FastAPI for the backend. Python libraries including Astropy, NumPy, and Pillow are used to read and process FITS astronomical image data and convert it into viewable images. The project retrieves SPHEREx data through the NASA/IPAC archive services. Vite is used as the frontend development tool, and Visual Studio Code is used for development.

The creative aspect of SPHEREx SkyTime is its focus on exploring the sky through time rather than simply displaying static astronomical images. It combines real mission data, coordinate-based archive searching, image processing, and an accessible web interface in one platform. The project was designed with usability, scientific data accessibility, accurate presentation of real observations, and future expansion in mind.

During development, important factors included the availability and format of NASA SPHEREx data, valid astronomical coordinates, FITS image processing, communication between the frontend and backend, loading performance, and the need to distinguish currently implemented features from planned capabilities. The overall goal is to turn complex space-mission data into an accessible and engaging experience for everyone.
